answer.text: Flash: $10/month. Automatic PR reviews on every push. $5 of AI credit a month, about 400 reviews.
AIR: $29.99/month. Up to 3 team seats, $18 of AI credit a month. Everything in Flash plus the managed dashboard.

If the CLI itself crashes, it sends a crash report to our error-tracking provider, Sentry: the exception details and stack trace, the Aletheore, operating system and Python versions, and recent log lines, with your home directory replaced by ~ and command-line arguments, the machine name and local variables removed. An exception message can still name a file or path from the project you were scanning. Nothing is sent unless the CLI crashes. Crash reporting is on by default; aletheore config crash-reporting off (or ALETHEORE_CRASH_REPORTING=0 ) turns it off.

Tree-sitter and git history produce air.json and air.toon. No LLM in the scan path and no account. A scan makes dependency advisory and license lookups and checks for a newer release, each of which can be turned off, and sends a crash report only if the CLI itself crashes.

Your source code and the evidence aletheore scan produces stay on your machine. Evidence is written to .aletheore/ in the repository you scanned, and a scan never uploads your source code. The CLI reports no usage data.

The CLI does contact a few services on its own. By default a scan looks up public advisory and license data for your dependencies, which sends dependency names and versions (not your code) to OSV.dev and to the package registries; --no-check-vulnerabilities and --no-check-licenses turn those lookups off. It also checks PyPI for a newer release; ALETHEORE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 turns that off.

An exception message can still name a file or path from the project you were scanning. Nothing is sent unless the CLI crashes. Crash reporting is on by default; aletheore config crash-reporting off (or ALETHEORE_CRASH_REPORTING=0 ) turns it off.

Aletheore is a small, early-stage team. We do not currently hold a SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar third-party compliance certification, and we don't claim to. If that's a hard requirement for your organization, tell us, it's useful signal for what to prioritize next.
